records.rule: Keep exact source-IP rejection before HELLO parsing and before cryptographic work; an unknown address should reveal as little protocol surface as practical.
Reject that reasoning. IP is an admission fact only; require the PSK-authenticated peer handshake and later receiver authority.
Apply both OCI /32 network filtering and Queue Fabric exact-IP peer binding. Neither replaces the other.

records.trigger: Considering encryption of all internal queue operations
records.rule: Keep confidentiality at the remote socket boundary unless another boundary independently requires it; in-process queue semantics are unchanged.

records.trigger: Allocator considers node lacking secure transport
records.rule: When the job requires secure remote dispatch, absence of QUEUE_SECURE_TRANSPORT_V2 is hard ineligibility; capacity/fitness/cost cannot compensate.

records.trigger: A delivery is retried on a fresh legitimate connection
records.rule: Cryptographic session replay separation and durable transferId idempotence solve different problems; retain both.

records.trigger: Optimising by reusing one authenticated TCP connection for many commands
records.rule: Do not reuse the current single derived nonce repeatedly. Design a sequence/nonce construction and version/qualify the protocol first.

records.trigger: Moving endpoint configuration into production wiring
records.rule: Resolve PSK via Secret Broker reference at the trusted runtime boundary; do not put raw keyHex in allocator, NoSQL, logs, command lines or durable definitions.

records.trigger: Describing security properties to operators or reviewers
records.rule: State confidentiality/integrity/mutual PSK authentication/transcript binding, but explicitly state no forward secrecy for dev5.
Treat wire identity and durable persistence identity as separate versioning axes; do not rewrite durable records merely because queue.transport advances.
Rebuild aggregate pre-auth source set from current peer table so stale addresses lose admission immediately.
Project identity, counters and health evidence, never raw secret material; keyId is safe metadata but not authority.

provenance.claim: Durable reasoning records summarize explicit transport doctrine.
Qualification and boundary record grounds failure, allocator and secret rules.
